steps: Set the bench so your ankles sit under the pads and your thighs lie flat on the top pad.
Fold your arms across your chest and keep your back straight.
Bend at the waist toward the floor.
Rise slowly until your body is straight.
Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Hold the bar with your palms up, hands shoulder width apart.
Bending only your elbows, curl the bar to your upper chest.
Pause, then lower it slowly until your arms are straight.
bicep-curl.note: Keep your hips and back still. No swinging.

steps: Stand tall and hold the bar at arm's length, hands just wider than your shoulders.
Let your shoulders drop as low as they go.
Lift your shoulders as high as you can.
Pause, then lower them slowly.
Rest the bar across your upper back and step away from the rack.
Stand with your feet slightly wider than your shoulders, toes turned out a little.
Bend your knees and hips as if sitting down, keeping your chest up.
Go as low as you can control, with your heels on the floor.
Push through your heels to stand up.
Sit on a bench with your hands beside your hips and your feet on a second bench.
Slide your hips off the edge and straighten your arms.
Bend your elbows to lower your body until your upper arms are level with the floor.
Press back up.
bench-dips.note: Do not go below a right angle at the elbow. It strains the shoulders.

steps: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor.
Hold the bar a little wider than your shoulders and lift it over your chest.
Lower the bar until it just touches your chest.
Press it back up until your arms are straight.
Lie on your back with your hands beside your head.
Lift your legs, knees bent and shins level with the floor.
Bring your left elbow to your right knee as your left leg straightens.
Switch sides in a steady pedalling motion.
air-bike.note: Twist from your stomach, not your neck.

steps: Set the pulleys at shoulder height or higher and hold one handle in each hand.
Stand in the middle with one foot in front of the other.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and bring your hands together in front of your chest.
Hold for a moment, then let your arms open slowly.
Stand with your toes on the footpad and your shoulders under the pads.
Rise onto the balls of your feet as high as you can.
Hold for a moment, then lower your heels slowly.
Grip the parallel bars and push up until your arms are straight.
Lean forward a little and bend your elbows to lower your chest.
Go down until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Press back up.
Hold the bar with your palms facing each other.
Hang with your arms straight.
Pull yourself up until your chin is above the bar.
Lower yourself slowly.
Kneel on the floor, put your hands together under your chest and lift up onto your toes.
Keep your back and neck in a straight line.
Bend your arms to lower your body until you nearly touch the floor.
Press back up.
Sit on the end of a bench with your legs apart and a dumbbell in one hand, palm up.
Press your elbow against your inner thigh.
Curl the dumbbell toward your chest.
Lower it slowly, then switch arms.
concentration-curls-with-dumbbell.note: Keep everything still except the working arm.

steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat or up on a bench.
Put your hands across your chest or beside your head.
Lift your head and shoulders off the floor, squeezing your stomach.
Hold for a moment, then lower slowly.
crunches.note: Keep your lower back on the floor.

steps: Stand with your feet under the bar, shoulder width apart.
Bend at the hips and knees with a flat back and grip the bar just outside your legs.
Stand up, keeping the bar close to your body.
Bend the same way to lower the bar to just above the floor.
Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand and your feet on the floor.
Press the dumbbells up over your chest.
Lower them slowly until your elbows are bent at a right angle.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, arms at your sides, palms forward.
Keep your elbows by your sides and curl the weights to your shoulders.
Lower them slowly until your arms are straight.
Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and a dumbbell in each hand.
Bend at the hips with a flat back, lowering the weights down your legs.
Stop just above the floor.
Stand back up, keeping the weights close to your body.
Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand and your arms straight up over your chest.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and lower the weights out to the sides in an arc.
Stop when you feel a stretch in your chest.
Bring them back up the same way.
Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, feet slightly wider than your shoulders.
Bend your knees and hips as if sitting down, keeping your chest up.
Go as low as you can control, heels on the floor.
Push through your heels to stand up.
squats-using-dumbbells.note: New to squats? Practise without weights first.

steps: Stand facing a bench or box with a dumbbell in each hand.
Step up with your left leg and bring your right leg up to meet it.
Step down the same way.
Repeat, starting with the other leg.
step-ups-with-dumbbells.note: Use a light weight until the movement feels steady.

steps: Lie face down with your hips on the edge of a bench and hold on with your hands.
Let your legs hang down.
Squeeze your glutes and kick one leg up and back.
Alternate legs in a steady rhythm.
Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your thighs.
Keep your arm straight and raise one weight to just above shoulder height.
Pause, lower it slowly, then switch arms.
Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.
Squeeze your glutes and lift your hips until your body makes a straight line.
Hold for a moment, then lower slowly.
Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Keep your elbows by your sides and curl the weights toward your shoulders.
Lower them slowly.
Lie on a bench set to about 45 degrees.
Hold the bar a little wider than your shoulders and lift it over your upper chest.
Lower the bar until it just touches your chest.
Press it back up until your arms are straight.
Sit on a bench set to about 45 degrees and hold the dumbbells at shoulder height.
Press them up over your chest, bringing them closer together.
Lower them slowly to your shoulders.
Lie under a bar set at chest height and hold it with your arms straight.
Keep your body straight, heels on the floor.
Pull your chest up to the bar.
Lower yourself slowly.
Sit upright and hold the bar with your palms facing you, hands shoulder width apart.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Let it rise slowly until your arms are straight.
Stand with a dumbbell at each side, palms facing your body.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and raise your arms out to the sides.
Stop at shoulder height, palms facing the floor.
Lower them slowly.
Lie face down on the machine with your heels under the pad.
Hold the grips and curl your heels toward your back.
Hold for a moment, then lower slowly.
Set the seat so the pad sits just above your ankles.
Hold the handles and keep your back against the seat.
Straighten your legs slowly without locking your knees.
Hold for a moment, then lower slowly.
Sit in the machine with your feet shoulder width apart on the plate.
Press the plate and release the safety locks.
Bend your knees to lower the weight, keeping your knees in line with your feet.
Press back up without locking your knees.
Lie on a bench with your hands under your hips and your legs off the end.
Keep your legs straight and raise them until they point at the ceiling.
Lower them slowly, stopping just above the bench.
Stand with a dumbbell in each hand. Beginners can use no weights at all.
Take a long step forward, keeping your body upright.
Lower your back knee until it is just above the floor.
Push off your front foot to step back, then switch legs.
Sit on a bench with your back straight and hold the bar at shoulder height, hands shoulder width apart.
Press the bar overhead until your arms are almost straight.
Pause, then lower it slowly to your shoulders.
Hold the bar with your palms facing away, hands wider than your shoulders.
Hang with your arms straight and your chest up.
Pull yourself up until your chin is above the bar.
Lower yourself slowly.
pull-up.note: Too hard at first? Use a band, or jump up and lower yourself slowly.

steps: Put your hands on the floor, shoulder width apart, and straighten your legs onto your toes.
Keep your head, back and hips in one straight line.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
push-up.note: Too hard at first? Put your knees on the floor.

steps: Stand holding the bar against your thighs, hands a little wider than your hips.
Keep your knees slightly bent and your back flat.
Push your hips back and slide the bar down your legs.
Stop when you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, then stand back up.
Set the machine so the pad sits just above your heels.
Sit upright with your legs in front of you.
Curl your legs back and hold for a moment.
Let them straighten slowly.
Sit with your feet on the footrests and your knees slightly bent.
Lean forward a little, back straight, and hold the handle.
Pull it to your stomach while sitting upright, elbows close to your body.
Let your arms straighten slowly.
Lie on your side with your legs straight and your forearm on the floor.
Lift your hips until your body makes a straight line.
Hold, then lower slowly and switch sides.
Lie on your stomach with your arms stretched out in front of you.
Lift your arms and legs off the floor.
Hold for 2 seconds, then lower.
Stand over the bar with one foot on each side and hold the handles.
Bend at the waist until your chest is nearly level with the floor, knees slightly bent.
Pull the bar toward your chest as high as you can.
Pause, then lower it slowly.
Grip the parallel bars and push up until your arms are straight.
Keep your body upright and your elbows close to your sides.
Lower yourself until your upper arms are level with the floor.
Press back up.
Stand tall and hold one dumbbell in both hands over your head.
Keep your upper arms still and lower the weight behind your head.
Raise it back up until your arms are straight.
Put your left knee and left hand on a bench, back level, with a dumbbell in your right hand.
Hold your right upper arm close to your body with your elbow bent.
Straighten your arm backward.
Bend it slowly, then switch arms.
Stand at a cable machine with a short bar on the high pulley, palms facing down.
Keep your elbows at your sides and your back straight.
Push the bar down until your arms are straight.
Let it rise slowly to chest height.
